title: Finalytics data types
description: The types exchanged between the Finalytics engine and its Python and JavaScript bindings.

name.description: A display name.

lot_method.description: How sales in this account choose lots, unless a sale says otherwise.

classifications.description:
Classifications by scheme, for grouping accounts: for example `owner: Alice` or
`wrapper: ISA`.

taxable.description:
Whether gains are taxed when they are realised: true by default. A retirement account,
or another tax-deferred or tax-exempt account, is not taxable, so rebalancing estimates
no tax on its sales.

Account.description: An account in a portfolio, such as a brokerage or custody account.

name.description: The account's name, if it has one.

value_base.description: The account's value in the base currency.

weight.description: The share of the portfolio's value.

AccountId.description:
Identifies an account within a portfolio.

Identifiers are non-empty, have no leading or trailing whitespace, and are compared
exactly (case matters).

values.description: The account's value at the end of each date, in the base currency.

flows.description:
The external flows into the account since the previous date (deposits and transfers in
positive; withdrawals and transfers out negative), each converted at its own date's rate.

AccountLine.description: One account's values and external flows on each date of an `AccountSeries`.

lines.description: One line per account, in the portfolio's order.

warnings.description: Prices and rates carried forward from earlier dates.

AccountSeries.description:
Each account's values and external flows on a set of dates: the input to performance by
account and by group of accounts.

name.description: The account's name, or its identifier.

taxable.description: Whether its gains are taxed when realised.

turnover.description: The value traded as a share of its value.

realised_gain_base.description: The gain its sales realise, after fees.

long_term_gain_base.description: With tax rates, the part of that gain from lots held long-term.

tax_base.description: With tax rates and a taxable account, the estimated tax on its sales.

warnings.description:
What to check before making the trades: carried prices, a shortfall of cash, and trades
left out.

AccountTrades.description: One account's part of a rebalance.

name.description: The account's identifier, the group's name, or "household".

value_start.description: The value at the start of the period, in the base currency.

value_end.description: The value at the end of the period.

flows.description: The external flows over the period, net: positive when more came in than went out.

weight_start.description:
The share of the household's value at the start, absent if the household started with
nothing.

time_weighted.description:
The time-weighted return over the period, absent when it cannot be measured, such as for
an account that gained or lost value on a day it started with none.

money_weighted.description:
The money-weighted return (annualised internal rate of return), absent when it cannot be
found.

contribution.description:
The contribution to the household's time-weighted return: each day's gain over the
household's starting value for the day, linked by the household's growth. The
contributions of all accounts add up to the household's return.

AccountsPerformance.description: The performance of one account, a group of accounts or the whole household over a period.

oneOf.description: `amount` (in `currency`) moved into `holding` (negative: out of it).

amount.description: The amount, net of tax withheld.

oneOf.description: `amount` (in `currency`) earned by `holding` and paid out to cash, such as a dividend.

`amount` (in `currency`) paid out of cash for a fee or a tax charged to the account
rather than to a holding: a cost of the portfolio, not a loss on the cash.

from.description: The instrument given up, wholly or in part.

oneOf.description:
`quantity` units of `to` replaced part of `from` (a spin-off, merger or symbol change);
the value moved is the market value of the new units on the date.

Allocation.description:
How a transaction moved value between holdings, used to measure each holding's
contribution. Value moved between holdings nets to zero; only external flows and expenses
change the portfolio's total.

risk_share.description:
Its share of the portfolio's risk: of its variance (its weight times its covariance with
the portfolio, over the portfolio's variance), or for minimum CVaR of its expected
shortfall (its weight times its mean loss in the worst periods, over the expected
shortfall).

fraction.description: As a fraction of the portfolio's value.

value.description: As an amount in the base currency.

Amount.description: A figure as a fraction and as an amount of money, such as a value at risk.

what.description: What is changed, such as "Monthly saving".

flow.description:
The flow changed, by its place in the plan's flows; absent for the start value or the
goal's amount.

to.description: The amount that gives the chance wanted, the rest of the plan as it is.

AmountChange.description: A change of an amount that reaches, or keeps, the chance wanted.

AssetBound.description: Limits on one asset's weight, in place of the default bounds.

intercept.description:
The intercept: the regression's alpha, or the mean return for a statistical model;
absent for a fundamental model.

r_squared.description:
The share of the asset's return variance the factors explain. Absent when the asset's
returns do not vary.

AssetFit.description: How well a factor model explains one asset's returns over the estimation period.

assets.description: The assets in the group; or give `classification`.

classification.description:
A classification scheme of the assets, such as `asset_class`: the group is the assets
classed as its name under it.

min.description: The smallest total weight: 0 by default.

max.description: The largest total weight: 1 by default.

AssetGroup.description:
A group of assets whose total weight is limited: the assets listed, or those classed as the
group's name under a classification, such as the group "Equity" under `asset_class`.

statistics.description: Its statistics, annualised with the assets' periods per year and risk-free rate.

tail_risk.description: Its value at risk and expected shortfall over one period at 95%, from history.

AssetStatistics.description: One asset's statistics, with its value at risk and expected shortfall at 95% (historical).

portfolio_return.description: The portfolio's return over all the periods, compounded.

benchmark_return.description: The benchmark's return over all the periods, compounded.

excess_return.description: `portfolio_return - benchmark_return`, which the linked effects add up to.

segments.description:
Each segment's effects over all the periods, linked, in the order the segments first
appear.

allocation.description: The allocation effects of all the segments, linked.

selection.description: The selection effects of all the segments, linked.

interaction.description: The interaction effects of all the segments, linked.

periods.description: Each period's own attribution, before linking.

Attribution.description: Brinson–Fachler attribution over one or more periods.

scheme.description:
The instrument classification scheme that defines the segments, such as `asset_class`.
Cash is the segment "cash", and instruments without the classification "unclassified".

periods.description:
The benchmark's segments in each period, such as each month. Without them, they are
derived from a blended benchmark: one period for each calendar month of the report, each
segment's weight the sum of its holdings' weights and its return their weighted return
over the month, by the classification `scheme` of the portfolio's instruments.

linking.description: How the periods are linked: Cariño's method by default.

AttributionInputs.description: What the attribution report compares the portfolio with.

start.description: The start of the period.

end.description: The end of the period.

AttributionPeriod.description:
The segments over one period. The portfolio weights add up to one, as do the benchmark
weights.

scheme.description: The classification scheme of the segments.

periods.description:
Each period's segments: the portfolio's weights and returns from its books, beside the
benchmark's.

attribution.description:
The attribution, by period and linked: the totals for a waterfall chart, and each
period's effects for a chart over time.

time_weighted.description:
The portfolio's time-weighted return over the same span, for comparison with the
attribution's portfolio return (`sum w r` in each period, linked), which leaves out
trading within each period.

results.description: The raw results: every return and trade, in and out of sample.

Backtest.description:
A backtest: the backtest report on one allocation against its benchmark, and the raw
results. Printing it prints the report, and showing it shows the report as a page.

digest.description:
A SHA-256 digest of the assets' returns and the settings, in hexadecimal: the same
inputs give the same report.

assets.description: The assets the strategies hold, other than the risk-free asset.

risk_free_asset.description: The risk-free asset, held as cash, if one of the assets is.

periods_per_year.description: The number of periods in a year.

covariance.description: The covariance estimator of the optimisations.

mean_returns.description: The estimator of the optimisations' mean returns.

limits.description: The limits on the weights, in words.

start.description: The date the first period of the data ends on.

end.description: The date the last period of the data ends on.

test_start.description: The first period the strategies are scored on.

test_end.description: The last period the strategies are scored on.

fit_end.description: For a holdout, the last period the weights were fitted to.

window.description: For walk-forward validation, the periods of history before the first fit.

risk_free_rate.description: The annual risk-free return over the test, compounded from the periods' returns.

origin.description: The date the first period of the data starts from, when it is known.

start_value.description: The value each run starts with, when the backtest follows money.

flows.description: Money paid in or taken out on dates, when the backtest follows money.

BacktestContext.description:
What a backtest report describes: the data, how the strategies were tested, and the digest
of the inputs.

strategies.description: The strategies, in the order of the results.

validation.description: How the strategies are validated: in sample by default.

rebalance.description: When the portfolio trades back to its targets: quarterly by default.

trading_cost_bps.description: The cost of trading, in basis points of the value traded: 10 is 0.1%.

benchmark.description: What the strategies are compared with, if anything.

start_value.description:
The value each run starts with, to follow money as well as returns: the reports then
give each run's ending value and money-weighted return. Zero, with flows, if absent.

flows.description:
Money paid in (positive) or taken out (negative) on dates, at the end of the period each
falls in, after its return.

BacktestOptions.description: What a backtest tests and how.

benchmark.description: The benchmark, if one was given, held alike.

history.description: For a holdout, both periods together, in sample then out of sample.

held.description:
The weights held in each period of the test, by asset: the largest few, then the rest
together, then cash; at the same dates as the growth.

name.description:
The report's title, such as "Maximum Sharpe, fitted to 2016": shown when it is printed
or laid out as a page.

BacktestReport.description: One allocation, tested against its benchmark: the backtest report.

dates.description: The date each period of the data ends on.

cash.description: The return of cash in each period: the risk-free return.

periods_per_year.description: The number of periods in a year.

strategies.description: Each strategy, in the order given.

benchmark.description: The benchmark, if one was given.

BacktestResults.description:
The result of a backtest: every strategy, and the benchmark if one was given, on the same
assets and dates.

name.description: The name in the results: `Benchmark` by default.

weights.description: The weights, by asset, adding up to one.

oneOf.description: Fixed weights by asset, held and rebalanced as the strategies are, with the same costs.

name.description: The name in the results: the column's by default.

oneOf.description:
An index or fund, by its prices: one column, with a price on or before each date of the
assets and one before the first.

Benchmark.description: What the strategies are compared with.

start.description: The start of the period.

end.description: The end of the period.

segments.description: The segments, with weights adding up to one.

BenchmarkPeriod.description: The benchmark's segments over one period.

name.description: The segment: a classification of the scheme, such as `Equity`.

benchmark_weight.description: The benchmark's weight in the segment at the start of the period.

benchmark_return.description: The benchmark's return in the segment over the period.

BenchmarkSegment.description: One segment of the benchmark over one period.

upper.description: The upper edge, excluded (included for the last bin).

count.description: The number of observations in the bin.

share.description: The share of all observations in the bin.

normal_share.description:
The share a normal distribution with the observations' mean and standard deviation puts
in the bin, for comparison.

covariance.description:
The covariance matrix of the assets' returns, in the units of the returns wanted, for
example annualised.

views.description: The views; without any, the posterior returns are the prior.

tau.description:
The uncertainty of the prior relative to the covariance, greater than zero: 0.05 by
default.

BlackLitterman.description: The inputs to the Black–Litterman model.

labels.description: The asset labels, in the order of the covariance matrix.

posterior_returns.description: The posterior expected returns, which blend the prior with the views.

posterior_covariance.description:
The covariance of returns given the views, `C + M`, where `M` is the posterior uncertainty
of the expected returns (He and Litterman, 2002).

view_variances.description: The variance of each view, in the order of the views.

BlackLittermanEstimate.description: The posterior of the Black–Litterman model.

min.description: The smallest weight allowed; negative for a short position.

Bound.description: Lower and upper limits on a weight.

by.description: The dimension: "holding", "currency", "kind", "account", or a classification scheme.

Breakdown.description: A whole split into parts by one dimension, such as by currency or by asset class.

start.description: The date the year's first period ends on.

end.description: The date the year's last period ends on.

complete.description: Whether the run covers the whole year.

CalendarReturn.description: The return over one calendar year, or the part of it in the run.

CashBalance.description: A cash balance in one account and currency.

date.description: The date: the money moves at the end of the period it falls in.

amount.description: The amount: positive paid in, negative taken out.

CashFlow.description: Money paid into a backtest's runs (a positive amount) or taken out (a negative one) on a date.

fx_rate.description: Units of base currency per unit of `currency`.

value_base.description: The balance in the base currency.

CashValue.description: A cash balance valued on a date.

anyOf.description: Text, or a date as text.

Cell.description: One cell of a `ReportTable`: a number, text, yes or no, or nothing.

to_reach.description: Whether the changes reach the chance wanted (true) or keep it (false).

amount.description: The goal's amount: the target, or each payment.

date.description: The target's date, or the month of the first payment, saving until then.

Changes.description:
What would change the outcome, one change at a time on the same simulations: below the
chance wanted, the smallest change that reaches it; at or above it, the largest change the
plan could absorb and keep it. A change that no amount within reach achieves is absent.

key.description: A stable key for the column, such as `value_base`.

label.description: A heading for people, such as "Value (USD)".

oneOf.description: Text.
An ISO 8601 date, as text.
A number.
A whole number.
A fraction, to show as a percentage: 0.05 is 5%.
An amount of money in a currency.
Yes or no.

ColumnKind.description: What a column holds, so that an export can format it.

report.description: The comparison report: each method scored on the periods it was tested on.

results.description: The raw results: every return and trade of each method, in and out of sample.

Comparison.description:
A comparison: the comparison report on several methods backtested side by side, and the
raw results. Printing it prints the report, and showing it shows the report as a page.

strategies.description: Each method, in the order given.

benchmark.description: The benchmark, if one was given, tested alike.

name.description:
The report's title, such as "S&P 500 stocks": shown when it is printed or laid out as a
page.

ComparisonReport.description: Methods tested the same way, side by side: the comparison report.

largest.description: The largest instrument holdings, largest first, with their share of the value invested.

top_five.description: The share of the value invested in the five largest instruments.

top_ten.description: The share of the value invested in the ten largest instruments.

herfindahl.description:
The Herfindahl–Hirschman index of the instruments' shares of the value invested in
instruments, from 1/n (equal) to 1 (one instrument).

effective_holdings.description: `1 / herfindahl`: the number of equal holdings that would be as concentrated.

Concentration.description:
How concentrated the portfolio's instruments are. Every share is of the value invested in
instruments, cash aside, so that the figures agree with each other.

budget.description: The sum of the weights; 1 by default.

bounds.description: Bounds on every weight; `[0, 1]` by default.

asset_bounds.description: Bounds on particular assets, in place of `bounds`.

leverage.description: The largest gross exposure, `sum |w|`, for portfolios with short positions.

turnover.description: A turnover limit and trading costs.

factor_exposures.description: Limits on factor exposures; they need a factor model.

trades.description: Limits on the size and number of trades; they need the turnover's current weights.

min_return.description:
The smallest expected return, net of trading costs, in the units of the expected
returns: a floor for the objectives that do not use expected returns, such as minimum
CVaR.

min_effective_assets.description:
The smallest effective number of assets, `1 / sum w_i^2`, from 1 to the number of
assets: the constraint `sum w_i^2 <= 1 / k` of DeMiguel, Garlappi, Nogales and Uppal
(2009), which keeps the weights from concentrating in a few assets.

Constraints.description: The constraints on a portfolio. The default is fully invested and long-only.

contribution.description:
Its contribution to the portfolio's time-weighted return. Contributions of all holdings,
with what fees and taxes charged to the accounts took (see `Performance::expenses`), add
up to the portfolio's return over the period.

return_base.description: The holding's own return in the base currency, when it can be measured.

return_local.description: The holding's own return in its own currency, when it can be measured.

currency_effect.description: `return_base - return_local`: what currency movements added or took away.

average_weight.description: The holding's average share of the portfolio's value at the end of each day.

Contribution.description: What one holding added to the portfolio's return over a period.

volatility_scale.description: The factor every volatility is multiplied by. The default is 1.

correlation_shift.description:
How far every correlation moves toward one, from 0 (not at all, the default) to 1 (all
the way).

CorrelationStress.description: A stress of a covariance matrix: volatilities scaled and correlations moved toward one.

matrix.description:
The covariance matrix, labelled like the returns. Scale it to annualise, for example by
252 for daily returns.

shrinkage.description: The shrinkage intensity, between 0 and 1, for the shrinkage estimators.

observations.description: The number of returns per asset used.

CovarianceEstimate.description: An estimated covariance matrix, per period of the returns.

oneOf.description: The sample covariance, with divisor n - 1.

decay.description: The decay factor, between 0 and 1: 0.94 by default.

oneOf.description:
An exponentially weighted covariance: the return `k` periods before the latest has
weight proportional to `decay^k`, the weights sum to one, and deviations are taken from
the weighted mean. A decay of 0.94 for daily returns follows RiskMetrics.

The empirical covariance (divisor n) shrunk towards a multiple of the identity with the
intensity of Ledoit and Wolf (2004).

The empirical covariance (divisor n) shrunk towards a multiple of the identity with the
oracle approximating shrinkage intensity of Chen, Wiesel, Eldar and Hero (2010).

The empirical covariance (divisor n) shrunk towards the matrix with the same variances
and every correlation the average sample correlation, with the intensity of Ledoit and
Wolf (2004, "Honey, I shrunk the sample covariance matrix").

factors.description:
The number of components, between 1 and the smaller of the number of assets and of
returns less one.

oneOf.description:
A statistical factor model of the first `factors` principal components of the sample
covariance, with each asset's variance kept: the covariance the model implies.

The sample correlation with the eigenvalues of noise replaced by their average: those
below the Marchenko–Pastur edge `(1 + sqrt(n / t))^2` of a random correlation matrix
of `n` assets and `t` returns. The variances are the sample's.

The analytical nonlinear shrinkage of Ledoit and Wolf (2020): each eigenvalue of the
sample covariance (divisor t - 1) shrunk by a kernel estimate of the spectral density,
for many assets against few returns.

CovarianceMethod.description:
How a covariance matrix is estimated from returns.

In JSON it is an object with a `type`, such as `{"type": "ewma", "decay": 0.97}`, or the
type's name alone, such as `"ledoit_wolf"`; an exponentially weighted covariance without a
decay has 0.94.

measured.description: Those measured with the history the rules and the sort need.

too_short.description: Those measured with too short a history.

stale.description: Those whose last close is too old: listed, but not measured.

matched.description: The matches kept: those that passed, within the limit.

lacking.description:
For each measure of the results' `measures`, how many securities that are not stale
have no value of it.

lacking_history.description:
For each measure, how many of those without a value have too short a history for it,
such as two years of closes for the 3-year return.

Coverage.description: How many securities were measured and how many matched.

loss.description: The plan's return over it, in money of the day, such as -0.26.

placed.description: The first month of the plan it is placed at.

CrashWindow.description: The worst run of twelve months in the history, for the plan's weights.

Currency.description: An ISO 4217 currency code, for example "USD".

portfolio_return.description: The portfolio's return in the base currency over all the periods, compounded.

benchmark_return.description: The benchmark's return in the base currency over all the periods, compounded.

excess_return.description: `portfolio_return - benchmark_return`, which the linked effects add up to.

currencies.description: Each currency's allocation effect, linked, in the order the currencies first appear.

periods.description: Each period's own attribution, before linking.

CurrencyAttribution.description: Currency attribution over one or more periods.

start.description: The start of the period.

end.description: The end of the period.

segments.description: The segments, with returns in their own currencies.

currencies.description: The returns of every currency of the segments, and of the base currency.

portfolio_exposures.description:
The portfolio's exposure to each currency after any hedging, adding up to one; without
it, each currency's share of the portfolio's segment weights (no hedging).

benchmark_exposures.description: The benchmark's exposure to each currency, as for the portfolio.

allocation.description:
`(u - v)(f - F)`, with `f` the currency's return including its interest rate and `F` the
benchmark's currency return.

CurrencyEffect.description: What one currency added to the excess return.

start.description: The start of the period.

end.description: The end of the period.

portfolio_return.description: The portfolio's return in the base currency.

benchmark_return.description: The benchmark's return in the base currency.

linking_coefficient.description:
The coefficient by which the period's effects are multiplied before they are added up
over the periods (one for a single period).

segments.description: Each segment's market effects, on returns in excess of its currency's cash return.

residual.description: What the model leaves out: the compounding of local and currency returns.

CurrencyPeriodAttribution.description: The currency attribution of one period.

spot_return.description:
The change in its value in the base currency, such as 0.02 when it gains 2% (0 for the
base currency).

cash_return.description: The return on cash in the currency over the period: its short-term interest rate.

CurrencyReturn.description: A currency's returns over a period.

name.description: The segment's name.

currency.description: The currency of the segment's assets.

portfolio_weight.description: The portfolio's weight in the segment at the start of the period.

portfolio_return.description: The return of the portfolio's holdings in the segment, in the segment's currency.

benchmark_weight.description: The benchmark's weight in the segment at the start of the period.

benchmark_return.description: The return of the benchmark's holdings in the segment, in the segment's currency.

CurrencySegment.description: A segment for currency attribution: its returns are in its own currency.

Date.description: A calendar date in ISO 8601 form, for example "2026-11-02".

Decimal.description: An exact decimal number. Finalytics writes decimals as strings, such as "201.50", and reads strings or numbers.

quote.description: The currency it is priced in.

DocumentFxRates.description: The rates for one currency pair in a portfolio document.

pivot.description: The currency through which FX rates are crossed; USD by default.

max_carry_days.description: How many days a price or rate may be carried forward; 5 by default.

prices.description: Prices by instrument, in each instrument's currency.

fx.description: FX rates: units of `quote` per unit of `base`.

DocumentMarketData.description: Market data stored in a portfolio document.

peak.description: The date of the peak the fall started from.

trough.description: The date of the lowest point.

recovery.description: The first date at or above the peak again, absent if the series has not recovered.

depth.description: The fall from the peak to the trough, as a negative return (-0.25 for a fall of 25%).

days_to_trough.description: Calendar days from the peak to the trough.

days_to_recovery.description: Calendar days from the trough to the recovery, if it happened.

Drawdown.description: One fall from a peak, to the trough and, if it happened, back to the peak.

value.description: The mean of the deepest `1 - confidence` of the drawdowns, as a positive fall.

DrawdownFigure.description: A conditional drawdown at risk: the mean of the deepest drawdowns of the cumulative returns.

oneOf.description: A lot was opened or changed; this is its new state.
A lot was closed.
Cash in one currency changed by `amount` (negative for a payment).

Effect.description: A change to the books made by one transaction.

index.description: Its position in the portfolio's transaction list.

allocations.description: How it moved value between holdings.

Event.description: One transaction as applied to the books.

ExcessReturn.description: A return compared with a benchmark's over the same dates.

exposure.description: The portfolio's exposure to the factor, `(B' w)_k`.

marginal.description:
The change in volatility per unit of exposure, `(F x)_k / volatility`. Absent when the
portfolio has no volatility.

component.description:
`exposure * marginal`. With the specific component, the components add up to the
volatility.

share.description: `component / volatility`. Absent when the portfolio has no volatility.

FactorContribution.description: One factor's share of a portfolio's volatility.

factor.description: The factor's name, as in the factor model.

benchmark.description:
Benchmark weights, one per asset. When given, the limits apply to the active exposure,
that of `weights - benchmark`.

FactorExposureLimit.description:
Limits on a portfolio's exposure to one factor of the problem's factor model, such as a beta
between 0.9 and 1.1 to the market factor or a neutral exposure to an industry.

oneOf.description: Time-series regression of each asset's returns on given factor returns.
Principal components of the sample covariance matrix.
Cross-sectional regression of each period's returns on given exposures.

FactorMethod.description: How a factor model was estimated.

exposures.description:
Each asset's exposure to each factor: one row per asset, one entry per factor, in the
order of the factor covariance matrix's labels.

factor_covariance.description: The covariance matrix of the factor returns, labelled with the factor names.

specific_variances.description: The variance of each asset's specific return, one per asset.

FactorModel.description:
A linear factor model of asset returns, `r = B f + e`: each asset's exposures `B` to a set of
factors, the covariance `F` of the factor returns, and the variance `d` of each asset's
specific return `e`, which is uncorrelated across assets and with the factors.

The model implies the covariance matrix `B F B' + diag(d)` for the assets. The factor
covariance and the specific variances share units, for example both daily or both
annualised.

model.description: The model, in the units of the returns (per period).

fit.description: The fit for each asset, in the model's order.

factor_returns.description:
The factor returns over the estimation period, one column per factor: the given factor
returns for a regression model, the principal component scores for a statistical model,
and the estimated factor returns for a fundamental model.

explained_variance.description: For a statistical model, each component's share of the total variance.

observations.description: The number of periods of returns used.

FactorModelEstimate.description: A factor model estimated from returns, with how well it fits each asset.

volatility.description: The volatility, `sqrt(x' F x + sum d w^2)`, in the units of the model.

factor_volatility.description: The volatility from the factors alone, `sqrt(x' F x)`.

specific_volatility.description: The volatility from specific returns alone, `sqrt(sum d w^2)`.

factors.description: Each factor's contribution, in the model's order.

specific_component.description: The specific part's contribution, `sum d w^2 / volatility`.

specific_share.description: `specific_component / volatility`. Absent when the portfolio has no volatility.

assets.description: Each asset's contribution under the model's covariance matrix, in the model's order.

FactorRisk.description:

HoldingLine.description:
One holding's values, trades and income on each date of a `HoldingSeries`.

trades across all lines add up to the portfolio's external flows plus its income. Fees and
taxes charged to an account rather than to a holding are expenses of its cash: they lower the
cash's value without being a loss on it, so a holding's gain on a date is its change in value
less its trades, plus its income and its expenses.
