holdings.description:
Each holding's weight before the trades, at the target and after, in the accounts
together: the largest target first, then cash.

accounts.description: Each account's trades, conversions, costs and warnings.

name.description:
The report's title, such as "Morgan family portfolio": shown when it is printed or laid
out as a page.

RebalanceReport.description:
The trades that move a portfolio's accounts to target weights: how each holding's weight
moves, what the trades change and cost, each account's trades, and what to check before
making them.

accounts.description: The proposal for each account with value, in the order given.

base_currency.description: The base currency, of the values below.

value_base.description: The accounts' combined value in the base currency.

weights_before.description: Each holding's weight in the combined value before the trades.

weights_after.description: Each holding's weight in the combined value after the trades.

turnover.description:
The one-way turnover of all the accounts: half the value traded, as a share of their
combined value.

realised_gain_base.description: The gain the sales would realise in the base currency, after fees.

fees_base.description: The fees of all the trades, in the base currency.

tax_base.description: With tax rates, the estimated tax on the sales' gains in the base currency.

kept_cash.description: The cash kept as it was, by currency, as `keep_cash` asked.

RebalanceResults.description:
The trades that move several accounts together to target weights of their combined value,
one proposal per account.

oneOf.description: At the end of each month.
At the end of each quarter (the default).
At the end of each year.

band.description:
The largest difference allowed between a weight and its target, such as 0.05 for
five percentage points.

oneOf.description: At the end of any period in which a weight is more than `band` away from its target.
Never: the portfolio buys its target weights once and holds them (buy and hold).

periods.description: The number of periods between rebalances, at least 1.

oneOf.description:
After every `periods` periods, counted from the first period of each run, such as 21
for daily returns traded about once a month.

RebalanceSchedule.description:
When the portfolio trades back to its target weights. Between trades the weights drift with
prices.

turnover.description: The value traded as a share of the combined value.

fees_base.description: The fees of all the trades.

realised_gain_base.description: The gain the sales realise, after fees.

long_term_gain_base.description: With tax rates, the part of the realised gain from lots held long-term.

tax_base.description: With tax rates, the estimated tax on the sales in taxable accounts.

unrealised_gain_base.description: The unrealised gain of the accounts before the trades.

before.description: Volatility and expected return a year before the trades.

RebalanceSummary.description:
The trades of a rebalance in figures: how many, how much is traded, what they cost and what
they change.

report.description:
The rebalance report: how the weights move, what the trades change and cost, each
account's trades, what to check, and how the trades were found.

results.description: The raw results: each account's trades, conversions, weights and costs.

Rebalancing.description:
A rebalancing: the rebalance report on the trades, and the raw results, each account's
proposal. Printing it prints the report, showing it shows the report as a page, and the
portfolio's `with_rebalance` makes the trades.

active_return.description: The annualised return less the benchmark's annualised return.

tracking_error.description: The annualised standard deviation of the active returns (returns less benchmark returns).

information_ratio.description: The annualised mean active return over the tracking error.

beta.description: The covariance of the returns with the benchmark's over the benchmark's variance.

alpha.description:
The mean return not explained by beta, in excess of the risk-free rate, annualised by
compounding: `(1 + mean(r - rf - beta (b - rf)))^periods_per_year - 1`.

correlation.description: The correlation of the returns with the benchmark's.

downside_beta.description:
The beta over the periods the benchmark fell: the slope of the returns on the
benchmark's in those periods alone. Absent with fewer than two such periods.

upside_beta.description: The beta over the periods the benchmark rose.

downside_capture.description:
The compound annual return over the periods the benchmark fell, over the benchmark's in
those periods: below 1, the portfolio lost less than the benchmark when it fell.

upside_capture.description: The same over the periods the benchmark rose: above 1, the portfolio gained more.

RelativeStatistics.description: Statistics of a returns series against a benchmark's returns over the same periods.

anyOf.description: An instrument, such as an index, by its identifier.

Weights by holding, adding up to one: instruments, such as funds or indices with prices,
and cash, such as `USD cash`.

ReportBenchmark.description:
The benchmark of the portfolio reports.

An instrument's levels are in its currency, as the portfolio's instruments give it (the base
currency for one they do not list), and are converted to the base currency at the market
data's rates. A blend holds its instruments, and any cash, at the weights given, rebalanced to
them at the start of each month, each in the base currency in the same way; the attribution
report derives the benchmark's segments from it.

oneOf.description: The holdings report.
The overview report.
The performance report.
The risk report.
The attribution report.
The scenarios report.

as_of.description: The date of the report: the last price date by default.

start.description: The first valuation date: the first transaction's date by default.

group_by.description:
Classification schemes of the instruments to break holdings, contribution and risk down
by, such as `asset_class` or `region`.

benchmark.description:
The benchmark: an instrument whose prices in the market data are its levels, such as an
index, which need not be held; or a blend of instruments by weight, such as
`{"VTI": 0.6, "BND": 0.4}`. Either is in the base currency, converted at the market
data's exchange rates.

risk_free_rate.description: The annual risk-free rate, for Sharpe ratios. The default is 0.

periods_per_year.description: Valuation periods in a year, for annualising: 252 (trading days) by default.

timing.description: When external flows happen within the day: at the start (the default) or the end.

covariance.description: How the covariance of the holdings' returns is estimated: Ledoit–Wolf by default.

confidences.description: The confidences of value at risk and expected shortfall: 0.95 and 0.99 by default.

rolling_window.description: The window of rolling statistics, in valuation periods: 63 by default.

histogram_bins.description: The number of bins of return histograms: 30 by default.

top.description:
How many holdings lists of the largest, the top contributors and the like show: 10 by
default.

long_term_after_days.description:
The holding period, in days, after which a lot or a gain is long-term: a lot held for
more than this many days is long-term, as in rebalancing's tax rates. 365 by default.

expected_returns.description:
Annual expected returns by instrument for the efficient frontier; instruments not listed,
and every instrument when none is, take their historical mean return.

frontier_points.description: The number of portfolios on the efficient frontier: 25 by default.

benchmark_weights.description: Benchmark weights by holding, for the ex-ante tracking error.

attribution.description: The benchmark's segments, for the attribution report.

scenarios.description: The scenarios of the scenarios report.

ReportOptions.description:
The options every report takes. Each report uses the ones that concern it; the others are
ignored, so one set of options can serve every screen.

name.description: A stable name, such as `holdings`, usable as a file or sheet name.

title.description: A title for people, such as "Holdings".

rows.description: The rows, one cell per column.

ReportTable.description: A table of a report: named, with typed columns and one row of cells per record.

objective.description: The objective each simulated problem was solved for.

weights.description: The average of the simulated problems' optimal weights, absent if none was solved.

weight_deviations.description:
The standard deviation of each weight across the simulated problems (divisor `m - 1` for
`m` solved problems), absent with fewer than two.

expected_return.description: The expected return of the average weights under the problem's own estimates.

volatility.description: The volatility of the average weights under the problem's own estimates.

max_violation.description: The largest amount by which the average weights break the problem's constraints.

solved.description: The number of simulated problems solved and averaged.

failed.description: The number of simulated problems the solver could not solve, left out of the average.

solve_time.description: The time taken, in seconds. It varies from run to run and is left out of comparisons.

samples.description: The number of simulated histories, at least 2; 100 to 500 is usual.

observations.description:
The number of periods in each simulated history, at least 2: the length of the history
the estimates came from, so that the simulated estimates are as uncertain as the real
ones.

seed.description:
The seed of the random numbers. The same seed gives the same result on every platform and
with any number of threads.

periods_per_year.description:
For estimates annualised from returns with this many periods in a year (12 for
monthly), the histories are simulated period by period, from the estimates divided by
it, and their estimates annualised again, so that they are as uncertain as estimates
from `observations` periods. Without it, each simulated period is in the estimates' own
units.

Resampling.description: How to resample a problem's estimates.

observations.description: The number of periods in each, as many as the returns the estimates came from.

solved.description: The number of simulated problems solved and averaged.

ResamplingSummary.description:
How resampled weights were found: the average of the optimal weights for histories simulated
from the estimates (Michaud, 1998).

size.description: The size of the ellipsoid, not negative.

covariance.description:
The covariance `S` of the estimation error, labelled like the problem; without one,
the problem's covariance matrix or factor model.

oneOf.description:
An ellipsoid around the estimates, `(mu - m)' S^-1 (mu - m) <= size^2`: the worst case
lowers a portfolio's expected return by `size * sqrt(w' S w)`. For estimates that are
sample means of `T` periods, `S` is the covariance divided by `T`, and `size^2` a
chi-squared quantile with as many degrees of freedom as assets.

half_widths.description: The half-width for each asset, not negative.

oneOf.description:
A box around the estimates, `|mu_i - m_i| <= half_widths_i`: the worst case lowers a
portfolio's expected return by `sum half_widths_i |w_i|`.

ReturnUncertainty.description:
Where the true expected returns may lie around the estimates, for robust mean–variance
optimisation.

ReturnsTable.description: The returns of several assets over the same periods, one column per asset.

label.description: The asset, as labelled in the covariance matrix.

marginal.description:
The change in the portfolio's risk per unit of weight: for volatility,
`(C w)_i / volatility`; for expected shortfall, the asset's mean loss in the tail
scenarios. Absent when the portfolio has no volatility.

component.description: `weight * marginal`. The components add up to the portfolio's risk.

share.description:
`component` over the portfolio's risk. The shares add up to one. Absent when the
portfolio has no risk.

RiskContribution.description: One asset's share of a portfolio's risk: its volatility, or its expected shortfall.

volatility.description:
The portfolio's volatility, `sqrt(w' C w)`, in the units of the covariance matrix (scale
the matrix to annualise).

contributions.description: Each asset's contribution, in the order of the covariance matrix.

RiskDecomposition.description: A portfolio's volatility split into each asset's contribution (Euler allocation).

value.description: The portfolio's value on the report's date.

returns.description: The portfolio's time-weighted returns, one per valuation period.

relative.description: Statistics against the benchmark, with a benchmark.

drawdown.description: The fall from the running peak on each valuation date.

tail.description:
Value at risk and expected shortfall by every method at every confidence of the
options.

histogram.description: The distribution of the returns, with the normal distribution's for comparison.

holdings.description: The current holdings' risk; absent (with a warning) when it cannot be estimated.

rolling.description:
Rolling annualised volatility, Sharpe ratio and, with a benchmark, beta and tracking
error.

RiskReturn.description: A portfolio's volatility and expected return, a year.

measure.description: The measure the rule tests, such as `"return_1y"`; or give `field`.

field.description: The field the rule tests, such as `"sector"` or `"pe_ratio"`; or give `measure`.

value.description: The number compared with, or `[low, high]` for `between`.

Rule.description:
A rule every match must meet: a measure or a numeric field compared with a number (`<`,
`<=`, `>`, `>=`) or a range (`between`), or a text field that is (`in`) or is not (`not_in`)
one of a list of values. A security without the value a rule tests fails it.

passed.description: How many securities that are not stale meet it.

lacking.description: How many that are not stale have no value of what it tests, and so fail it.

remaining.description: How many meet it and every rule before it.

RuleResult.description: A rule, with how many securities met it.

anyOf.description: A range: the lowest and the highest values.

RuleValue.description: The number a numeric rule compares with, or the `[low, high]` range of `between`.

dates.description: The date each period ends on.

returns.description:
The return of each period, net of the cost of the trades made at the end of the one
before.

start.description:
The weights bought at the start, by asset; what they leave is held in cash. The start
costs nothing.

Run.description: A strategy held over a run of periods, rebalanced on the schedule, net of trading costs.

start.description: The date the first period ends on.

end.description: The date the last period ends on.

statistics.description: Return, risk and ratios, against the risk-free return over the run.

tail_risk.description: Historical value at risk and expected shortfall over one period, at 95%.

risk_free_rate.description: The annual risk-free return over the run.

relative.description: Against the benchmark over the same periods, if there is one.

rebalances.description: The number of trades after the start.

turnover_per_year.description: The share of value bought (or sold) in a year.

costs_per_year.description: The cost of trading as a share of value in a year.

largest_trade.description: The largest trade, as a share of value bought.

growth.description:
The growth of 100, from 100 on the date the run enters (when it is known), at the end of
each month for daily or weekly returns, and of each period otherwise.

drawdown.description:
The fall from the highest value so far, from 0 on the date the run enters: the deepest
in each month for daily or weekly returns, and at each period otherwise.

rolling_sharpe.description:
The Sharpe ratio over the past three years, at the growth's dates once three years have
passed, when the run is longer than three years.

years.description: The return in each calendar year.

months.description: The return in each month, a row per year and a column per month.

money.description: The run followed with money, when the backtest follows it.

RunReport.description: One run of a strategy, summarised: its statistics, trading and the series its charts draw.

values.description: The value at the start of each of the recorded months, in today's money.

met.description: Whether this simulation meets the goal.

SamplePath.description: One simulation's value at each recorded month.

oneOf.description: Shocks to instruments, groups, currencies or factors.
A historical period.

ScenarioDefinition.description: What a scenario does: shocks, or a historical period replayed.

group_by.description:
Classification schemes to add the effect up by, such as `asset_class`. Instruments
without the classification are in the group "unclassified", and cash in "cash".

risk.description: The risk model for the risk before and after; without one, no risk is reported.

ScenarioOptions.description: What to report beyond the effect on each holding.

name.description: The scenario's name.

result.description: The result; absent when the scenario could not be run.

problems.description: The problems that stopped it, with paths into the scenario.

ScenarioOutcome.description: One scenario's result, or why it could not be run.

dates.description: Every date in the period with a price for a holding, and its start and end.

values.description: The holdings' value on each date, in the base currency.

worst_drawdown.description:
The largest fall from a peak over the period, absent if the value never falls or is not
always above zero.

ScenarioPath.description: The hypothetical value of today's holdings over a historical period.

holdings.description: Each holding, in holding order: instruments by identifier, then cash by currency.

not_shocked.description: The instruments held whose return in their own currency no shock set.

factor_returns.description:
The factor returns applied, given and propagated, in the order of the model's factors;
empty without factor shocks.

groups.description: The effect by each classification scheme the options group by.

risk_before.description: The risk before, with a risk model.

risk_after.description:
The risk after, with the stressed covariance if the risk model has a stress; absent
without a risk model or if the portfolio is worth nothing after.

path.description: For a historical scenario, the holdings' value over the period.

warnings.description: Prices and rates carried forward from earlier dates, and shocks that matched nothing.

ScenarioResult.description: What a scenario does to a portfolio.

volatility.description:
The volatility of the portfolio's return, in the units of the risk model (scale the
model to annualise).

value_at_risk_base.description:
The parametric value at risk of the portfolio's value at the model's confidence, a loss
in the base currency: `z * volatility * value`.

contributions.description: Each holding's contribution to the volatility, in the order of the holdings.

groups.description: The contributions added up by each classification scheme the options group by.

ScenarioRisk.description: A portfolio's risk before or after a scenario.

covariance.description:
The covariance of the holdings' returns, labelled with instrument identifiers and, for
cash, the currency code followed by " cash" (as holding returns are). Give this or
`factor_model`.

factor_model.description: A factor model of the holdings' returns, labelled in the same way.

confidence.description: The confidence of the value at risk. The default is 0.95.

stress.description: A stress of the covariance for the risk after the scenario, as in a crisis.

ScenarioRiskModel.description: The risk model for the risk before and after a scenario.

name.description: The scenario's name.

change.description: The change in value, in the base currency.

value_at_risk_after_base.description: The value at risk after, in the base currency, at the first confidence of the options.

stress.description: The stress of the covariance behind the risk after, if the scenario has one.

ScenarioSummary.description: One scenario in a line, for a summary table or a bar chart.

value.description: The portfolio's value before every scenario.

risk_start.description: The first date of the returns behind the risk model, when there is one.

scenarios.description: Each scenario, in the order given.

summary.description: The scenarios that ran, in a line each.

changes.description: The change in each holding's value (rows) in each scenario that ran (columns).

returns.description: Each holding's return in the base currency in each scenario that ran.

SchemeContributions.description: Contributions added up by the groups of one classification scheme.

SchemeImpact.description: The effect of a scenario by the groups of one classification scheme.

SchemePerformance.description: Performance by the groups of one classification scheme of the accounts.

groups.description: Each group's share of the volatility, in name order.

SchemeRisk.description: Risk by the groups of one classification scheme.

report.description:
The screening report: how the rules narrow the universe, the matches in order, the
securities that fail just one rule, where each threshold falls and every measure.

results.description:
The raw results: one row per security, with each measure's value, its fields and
whether it matched.

Screen.description:
A screen: the screening report and the raw results. Printing it prints the report, and
showing it shows the report as a page.

name.description: The measure's or the field's name, such as `"return_1y"` or `"sector"`.

label.description: Its name in words, such as "1-year return" or "Sector".

unit.description: How a measure is shown; absent for a field.

field.description: Whether it is a field rather than a measure.

ScreenColumn.description: A column of the matches: a measure or a field.

digest.description:
A SHA-256 digest, in hexadecimal, of the options and of what the screen found for each
security: the same inputs give the same report.

first_date.description: The earliest close of any security.

max_carry_days.description: The most days a last close could be before the date measured to without being stale.

fields.description: The names of the fields given.

warnings.description: Problems that did not stop the screen.

ScreenContext.description: What a screen measured, beside its figures: what the report needs to describe it.

late.description:
The securities measured on a last close before the date measured to, within
`max_carry_days` of it.

stale.description: The stale securities: listed, but not measured.

too_short.description: The securities with too short a history for a rule or the sort.

common_start.description: The date of every security's first close, when they all share one.

ScreenExceptions.description: What is out of the ordinary in the securities' prices.

rank.description: Its place in the sort, from 1.

values.description: Its value in each column, in the order of the report's `columns`.

near_threshold.description:
The places in `columns` of its values close to a threshold of a rule: within 10% of it
or, for a threshold of zero, within 10% of the measure's typical size, the median of its
size across the securities that are not stale.

ScreenMatch.description: One security of the matches, with its value in each of the report's columns.

as_of.description: The date measured to: the latest date in the universe by default.

max_carry_days.description:
The most days a security's last close may be before `as_of`; a security whose last close
is older is stale: listed, but not measured. 5 by default.

measures.description:
The measures to compute, by name, such as `["return_1y", "rsi_14"]`: by default every
measure the universe allows (those against a benchmark need one, and those of volumes
and dividends need them). The measures the rules and the sort use are computed too.

rules.description: The rules a security must all meet to match.

sort.description: How the matches are sorted; in the universe's order by default.

limit.description: The most matches to keep, after sorting.

ScreenOptions.description:
What a screen measures and keeps. Everything is optional: by default every measure the
universe allows, on its latest date, with no rules.

coverage.description: How many securities were measured, passed and matched.

rules.description: Each rule, with how many met it.

also_passed.description: The first securities that pass every rule but are beyond the limit, in order: up to ten.

near_misses.description:
Every security that fails just one rule, the closest to passing first: by how far its
value is from the rule's threshold, as a share of the threshold (or, for a threshold of
zero, of the measure's typical size). Those that fail a rule on text, or have no value
for it, come last.

strips.description:
For each measure or numeric field the rules compare with a number, every security's
value against the rules' thresholds.

spread.description: The spread of each measure across the universe.

exceptions.description: What is out of the ordinary in the securities' prices.

name.description:
The report's title, such as "Quality at a fair price": shown when it is printed or laid
out as a page.

ScreenReport.description: The screening report: what one screen of a universe found.

max_carry_days.description: The most days a last close could be before `as_of` without being stale.

risk_free_rate.description: The annual risk-free rate of the Sharpe and Sortino ratios.

measures.description: The measures computed, in the order of each security's `values`.

fields.description: The names of the fields given.

rules.description: Each rule, with how many met it.

coverage.description: How many securities were measured, passed and matched, and how many lacked each measure.

securities.description: One row per security, in the universe's order.

warnings.description: Problems that did not stop the screen, such as closes left out.

ScreenResults.description:
The raw results of a screen: one row per security, in the universe's order, with each
measure's value, its fields and whether it matched; the matches in order; each rule with how
many met it; and how many were measured.

oneOf.description: Measured, with the history every rule and the sort need.

Measured, but with fewer than two closes up to the date measured to, or without the
history a rule or the sort needs: it fails the rules it cannot be judged on.
Its last close is too long before the date measured to: listed, but not measured.

matched.description: Whether it is one of the matches kept: it passed, and is within the limit.

rank.description: Its place among the matches kept, from 1.

first_date.description: The date of its first close.

last_date.description: The date of its last close on or before the date measured to.

values.description:
Its value of each measure of the results' `measures`, in their order; absent where it
has none.

SecurityScreen.description: One security's row of a screen: its measures, its fields and whether it matched.

dates.description: The dates of its closes, in increasing order.

close.description:
Its close on each date. Adjusted closes, which include dividends and splits, give total
returns. A close that is not a number (NaN, or `null` in JSON) is no close: that date is
left out.

volume.description: The volume traded on each date, if known; NaN (`null`) where not.

dividends.description:
The dividend per share paid on each date, its ex-date, and zero on the others, if known;
NaN (`null`) where not known, which counts as none paid unless every one is unknown.

fields.description:
Values the library does not compute, by name, such as `{"sector": "Technology",
"pe_ratio": 18.4}`: numbers or text, for rules and results.

SecuritySeries.description:
One security's prices on its own dates: a close on each date, and its volume, dividends and
fields if known.

name.description: The segment's name.

portfolio_weight.description: The portfolio's weight in the segment at the start of the period.

portfolio_return.description: The return of the portfolio's holdings in the segment over the period.

benchmark_weight.description: The benchmark's weight in the segment at the start of the period.

benchmark_return.description: The return of the benchmark's holdings in the segment over the period.

Segment.description:
A segment of a portfolio and of its benchmark over one period: an asset class, a sector, a
region or any other grouping.

name.description: The segment's name.

allocation.description:
The effect of weighting the segment differently from the benchmark,
`(w - b)(s - B)`.

selection.description:
The effect of the portfolio's holdings in the segment returning differently from the
benchmark's, `b (r - s)`.

interaction.description: The joint effect of the two, `(w - b)(r - s)`.

SegmentEffects.description: What one segment added to the excess return.

name.description: What the series is, such as "Portfolio" or "Rolling volatility (63 days)".

Series.description: A labelled series of numbers over time, for a line or bar chart.

validation.description: How the strategies are validated: in sample by default.

rebalance.description: When the portfolio trades back to its targets: quarterly by default.

trading_cost_bps.description: The cost of trading, in basis points of the value traded: 10 is 0.1%. Zero by default.

oneOf.description: The input can be used, but the caller should know about this.
The input cannot be used as it is.

Severity.description: How serious a validation issue is.

oneOf.description: Its own shock.
A group shock.
The factor shocks and its exposures.
Its prices over a historical period.

instrument.description: The instrument whose prices were used.

oneOf.description: Another instrument's prices over a historical period.
Cash: only a change in its currency's value moves it.
Nothing: its return in its own currency is zero.

ShockSource.description: How a holding's return in a scenario was set.

instruments.description: Returns of single instruments, by identifier.

groups.description:
Returns of every instrument in a group. An instrument without its own shock may match at
most one of them.

currencies.description: Changes in the value of currencies in the base currency: -0.1 when a currency loses 10%.

Shocks.description:
The shocks of a scenario. An instrument's return in its own currency comes from its own
shock, or else from the one group shock that matches it, or else from the factor shocks; an
instrument none of them reaches returns zero and is listed as not shocked. A currency shock
compounds with the instrument's return, and applies to cash in that currency.

expected_shortfall.description:
The portfolio's expected shortfall over one period of the scenarios, as a positive loss:
the mean loss in the worst `1 - confidence` of them (the Rockafellar–Uryasev tail mean,
which minimum CVaR minimises).

contributions.description:
Each asset's contribution: its weight times its mean loss in those scenarios, in the
order of the scenarios' columns. The components add up to the expected shortfall.

ShortfallDecomposition.description:
A portfolio's expected shortfall split into each asset's contribution (historical Euler
allocation).

value.description: The mean loss in the worst `1 - confidence` of the periods, as a positive return.

ShortfallFigure.description: An expected shortfall over one period of the returns.

oneOf.description: A purchase.
A sale.

name.description: The part's name: a holding, a currency, a group.

value.description: Its value in the base currency.

Slice.description: One part of a whole, for a pie, bar or treemap chart.

weights.description: The optimal weights, one per asset, when the status is optimal or nearly optimal.

objective_value.description:
The value of the objective at the weights: the variance for minimum variance and target
return; the utility for mean–variance; the expected return for target volatility; the
Sharpe ratio; the diversification ratio; the CVaR, as a positive loss; the semivariance;
the CDaR, as a positive drawdown of the summed returns; for risk budgeting, the largest
difference between an asset's share of risk and its budget. Absent for hierarchical risk
parity, which optimises no objective. The downside measures are per period of the
scenarios.

expected_return.description: The expected return at the weights, when expected returns are given.

volatility.description: The volatility at the weights, when a covariance matrix or a factor model is given.

max_violation.description:
The largest amount by which the weights break a constraint (0 when every constraint
holds exactly).

iterations.description: Iterations of the solver or of Newton's method.

solve_time.description: The time taken, in seconds. It varies from run to run and is left out of comparisons.

Solution.description:
The result of an optimisation, with what is needed to judge it: the status, the objective,
how closely the constraints hold, and the work done.

Two solutions are equal when everything but the time taken is equal, so that solving the
same problem twice gives equal solutions.

oneOf.description: The Clarabel interior-point solver for convex conic programmes.
Newton's method on the convex risk-budgeting problem.
Hierarchical clustering and recursive bisection, without a solver.
A formula, without a solver: equal weight and inverse volatility.

The interior-point solver, followed by a heuristic for trade limits: trades below the
minimum, and the smallest trades beyond the largest number allowed, are left out and the
rest re-optimised, round by round. Not guaranteed to find the best portfolio within the
limits.

SolveMethod.description: The method that produced a solution.

oneOf.description: Solved to the solver's full accuracy.

Solved to reduced accuracy; the weights are usable but should be checked against the
solution's largest constraint violation, `max_violation`.
No portfolio satisfies the constraints.
The objective can be improved without limit; add bounds or a leverage limit.
The solver stopped at its iteration limit.

The solver could not make progress, usually because the inputs are badly scaled or
nearly degenerate.

measure.description: The measure sorted by; or give `field`.

field.description: The numeric field sorted by; or give `measure`.

order.description: The largest first (`descending`) or the smallest first (`ascending`).

Sort.description:
How matches are sorted: by a measure or a numeric field, one way or the other. Securities
without a value come last.

digest.description:
The SHA-256 digest, in hexadecimal, of the portfolio document with its market data, as
the engine writes it. The same inputs give the same digest in every language.

Source.description:
What a report was computed from: a digest of the portfolio document and market data, and
their size. Computing it once and passing it to each report avoids hashing the inputs again.

total_return.description: The compounded return over the whole series.

annualised_return.description: The compound annual growth rate: `(1 + total_return)^(periods_per_year / observations) - 1`.

volatility.description: The annualised standard deviation of the returns (sample, divisor n - 1).

downside_deviation.description:
The annualised root mean square of the shortfalls below the target return, over all
observations.

sharpe_ratio.description:
The mean return in excess of the risk-free rate over its standard deviation, annualised by
the square root of `periods_per_year`.

sortino_ratio.description: The annualised mean return in excess of the target over the downside deviation.

max_drawdown.description:
The largest fall from a peak, as a negative return (-0.25 for a fall of 25%), measured
from a starting value before the first return.

conditional_drawdown_at_risk.description:
The conditional drawdown at risk at 95%: the mean of the worst 5% of the drawdowns after
each return, as a negative return like `max_drawdown` (Chekhlov, Uryasev and Zabarankin,
2005). It is the Rockafellar–Uryasev tail mean, as the expected shortfall of minimum CVaR
is, of the drawdowns measured on the compounded value.

ulcer_index.description:
The Ulcer index: the root mean square of the drawdowns after each return, as a positive
fraction (Martin, 1987). It weighs how deep and how long the falls are.

calmar_ratio.description: The annualised return over the size of the maximum drawdown; absent without a drawdown.

skewness.description: The skewness of the returns (population moments).

excess_kurtosis.description:
The kurtosis of the returns less 3, so that a normal distribution has 0 (population
moments).

Statistics.description:
Statistics of a returns series.

Annualised figures scale by the number of periods in a year given in the options. Ratios
that divide by a dispersion are absent when the returns do not vary.

periods_per_year.description:
Return periods in a year: 252 for daily trading-day returns (the default), 52 for weekly,
12 for monthly.

risk_free_rate.description:
The annual risk-free rate for the Sharpe ratio and alpha. It is converted to a rate per
period by compounding: `(1 + rate)^(1 / periods_per_year) - 1`. The default is 0.

target_return.description:
The annual minimum acceptable return for downside deviation and the Sortino ratio,
converted to a rate per period in the same way. The default is 0.

oneOf.description: The chance is at least the one from which there is room to spare.
The chance is at least the one wanted.
The chance is up to 15 points below the one wanted.
The chance is more than 15 points below the one wanted.

Status.description: Where a plan stands against the chance wanted.

name.description: The name in the results; the method's own by default, such as `Maximum Sharpe`.

options.description: The method, its parameters and the limits on the weights.

oneOf.description:
An optimisation, refitted as the validation says. The limits of `options` apply to the
methods that take them; equal weight, inverse volatility, risk parity, risk budgeting
and hierarchical risk parity are fully invested and long only.

name.description: The name in the results: `Weights` by default.

oneOf.description: Fixed weights by asset, adding up to one. The risk-free asset, if named, is held as cash.

name.description: The strategy's name.

fitted.description:
Whether a method fitted the weights to returns: false for fixed weights and for the
benchmark.

tested.description:
The run the strategy is scored on: out of sample for a holdout or walk-forward
validation, in sample otherwise.

in_sample.description:
For a holdout or walk-forward validation, the run in sample: on the history before the
test for a holdout, and with weights fitted to the whole history over the same periods
as the test for walk-forward. Fixed weights have none, as they were not fitted; the
benchmark has the same periods as the strategies' run in sample, for reference.

weights.description: The weights bought at the start of the test, then at each refit.

failures.description: Each refit that found no weights, when the weights held were kept.

notes.description: Anything the reader should know about how the strategy was run.

StrategyReport.description: One strategy, scored on the periods it was tested on, with its weights over time.

name.description: The strategy's name.

fitted.description:
Whether a method fitted the weights to returns: false for fixed weights and for the
benchmark, which were not fitted to any history.

in_sample.description:
The returns of weights tested on the history they were fitted to; for fixed weights,
the same periods as a fitted strategy's.

out_of_sample.description: The returns of weights tested on history they had not seen.

failures.description: Each refit that found no weights, when the weights held were kept.

notes.description:
Anything the reader should know about how the strategy was run, such as limits that did
not apply to it.

StrategyResult.description:
One strategy's backtest.

`in_sample` holds the returns of weights fitted to the history they are tested on: the
whole history for in-sample validation; the history before the test for a holdout; and, for
walk-forward validation, the whole history, tested on the same periods as `out_of_sample`, so
that the two can be compared directly. `out_of_sample` holds the returns of weights tested on
history they had not seen; it is absent for in-sample validation.

matched.description: Whether it is one of the matches.

StripPoint.description: One security's value on a threshold strip.

oneOf.description:
From the observed returns: the quantile with linear interpolation between order
statistics, and the mean of the worst `floor((n - 1) * alpha) + 1` returns.
From a normal distribution with the sample mean and standard deviation.

From the normal quantile adjusted for skewness and excess kurtosis by the Cornish–Fisher
expansion. Expected shortfall integrates the Edgeworth expansion of the density to that
quantile (Boudt, Peterson and Croux, 2008), and is never less than the value at risk.

TailMethod.description: How the tail of the return distribution is estimated.

value_at_risk.description: The loss exceeded with probability `1 - confidence`.

expected_shortfall.description:
The expected loss when the value at risk is exceeded (also called conditional value at
risk).

shortfall_at_var.description:
Whether the expected shortfall was raised to the value at risk. The Cornish–Fisher
expansion can put the mean of the tail above its quantile when the excess kurtosis is
large; the expected shortfall is never below the value at risk, so it is set to it.

TailRisk.description:
Value at risk and expected shortfall over one period of the returns.

Both are losses, reported as positive returns: a value at risk of 0.021 at 95% confidence
means that one period in twenty is expected to lose 2.1% or more.

value_at_risk.description: The value at risk over one valuation period, a loss.

expected_shortfall.description: The expected shortfall over one valuation period, a loss.

shortfall_at_var.description:
Whether the expected shortfall was raised to the value at risk, as the Cornish–Fisher
expansion can need when the excess kurtosis is large.

TailRow.description: Value at risk and expected shortfall by one method at one confidence.

short_term.description: The rate on gains from lots held for at most `long_term_after_days` days.

long_term.description: The rate on gains from lots held for longer.

long_term_after_days.description: The holding period, in days, beyond which a gain is long-term: 365 by default.

TaxRates.description:
Tax rates on realised gains, for tax-aware sales. A lot held for more than
`long_term_after_days` days is long-term. The rates apply to gains in the base currency,
after fees; a loss saves tax at its rate.

name.description: The measure's or the field's name.

unit.description: How a measure is shown; absent for a field.

rules.description: The places in the report's `rules` of the rules that test it.

points.description: The value of every security that is not stale and has one, lowest first.

ThresholdStrip.description:
Where the securities' values of one measure, or of a numeric field, fall against the
thresholds of the rules that test it.

TimeSeries.description:
Values indexed by strictly increasing dates.

Construction checks the ordering, so every `TimeSeries` can be searched by date. A series is
serialised as `{"dates": [...], "values": [...]}`, and deserialising checks it again.

benchmark.description: The benchmark's weights, one per asset.

limit.description:
The largest tracking error allowed, `sqrt((w - b)' C (w - b))`, in the units of the
covariance matrix's volatility.

TrackingErrorLimit.description: A limit on ex-ante tracking error against a benchmark.

date.description: The date at whose end the trade is made.

weights.description: The weights after the trade, by asset; what they leave is held in cash.

turnover.description:
The share of the portfolio's value bought (or, equally, sold): half the sum of the
changes in weight, cash included.

cost.description: The cost of the trade as a share of the portfolio's value.

refit.description: Whether the weights were refitted, rather than restored.

Trade.description: A trade back to target weights, or to new ones after a refit.

minimum.description:
The smallest trade allowed, as a weight: each asset is either not traded or traded by at
least this much.

maximum_count.description: The largest number of assets traded.

TradeLimits.description:
Limits on the trades from the current portfolio (the turnover's current weights). They are
not convex, so the solver's portfolio is adjusted by a heuristic, reported as the method
`trade_elimination`, which is not guaranteed to find the best portfolio within the limits.

price.description: The price per unit, in the instrument's currency.

value_base.description: The value traded, in the base currency.

fees_local.description: The fee, in the instrument's currency.

realised_gain_base.description: For a sale, the gain it realises, after fees.

tax_base.description: For a sale in a taxable account with tax rates, the estimated tax.

turnover.description: The one-way turnover: half the sum of the absolute changes in weight, cash included.

count.description: The number of assets traded, cash aside.

trades.description: Each asset traded, and cash, the largest change first.

TradesSummary.description: The trades from the weights held now to the weights found.

id.description: The caller's identifier, unique within the portfolio.

account.description: The account the transaction belongs to.

trade_date.description: The date the transaction takes effect for positions and performance.

settle_date.description: The date cash settles, if different from the trade date.

oneOf.description: Buy `quantity` units at `price` per unit, paying `fees` on top.

quantity.description: The number of units, greater than zero.

price.description: The price per unit, zero or more.

fees.description: Commissions and other costs of the trade, added to the cost basis.

oneOf.description: Sell `quantity` units at `price` per unit, with `fees` deducted from the proceeds.

quantity.description: The number of units, greater than zero.

price.description: The price per unit, zero or more.

fees.description: Commissions and other costs, deducted from the proceeds.

lot_method.description: Overrides the account's lot method for this sale.

lots.description: The lots to close, for specific identification.

oneOf.description: Cash paid into the account from outside the portfolio.
Cash taken out of the portfolio.
Units received from outside the portfolio.

quantity.description: The number of units, greater than zero.

cost_basis.description:
The total cost basis carried over, in the instrument's currency. When absent, the
market value on the trade date is used.

acquired.description: The original acquisition date, when the holding period carries over.

oneOf.description: Units sent out of the portfolio. No gain is realised.

quantity.description: The number of units, greater than zero.

lot_method.description: Overrides the account's lot method for this transfer.

lots.description: The lots to send, for specific identification.

oneOf.description: A dividend received in cash.

withholding_tax.description: Tax withheld at source, in the same currency.

oneOf.description: Interest received in cash, from an instrument or on the cash balance.

instrument.description: The instrument that paid it, if any.

withholding_tax.description: Tax withheld at source, in the same currency.

oneOf.description: A fee not tied to a trade, such as a custody or management fee.
A tax not tied to a trade.
Cash converted from one currency to another.

A share split: every `from` units become `to` units, with cost basis unchanged. A reverse
split has `to` below `from`.

A spin-off: holders receive `ratio` units of a new instrument per unit held, and a share
`cost_allocation` (between 0 and 1) of the cost basis moves to the new units.

cost_allocation.description: The share of cost basis moved to the new units.

oneOf.description:
A merger or acquisition: each unit held becomes `ratio` units of `new_instrument`, plus
`cash_per_unit` in cash, which reduces the cost basis (gains beyond the basis are
realised).

ratio.description: New units per unit held; zero for an all-cash takeover.

cash_per_unit.description: Cash per unit held, in the held instrument's currency.

oneOf.description: The instrument's identifier changes; lots carry over unchanged.

A return of capital paid in cash, which reduces the cost basis (amounts beyond the basis
are realised as gains).

amount.description: The total amount, in the instrument's currency.

Transaction.description:
One event in the life of a portfolio.

Transactions are applied in trade-date order; transactions on the same date are applied in the
order given. Positions are booked on the trade date; the settlement date is recorded for cash
reporting.

TransactionId.description:
Identifies a transaction. Lots opened by a transaction take their identity from it.

Identifiers are non-empty, have no leading or trailing whitespace, and are compared
exactly (case matters).

current.description: The current weights, one per asset.

limit.description:
The largest one-way turnover, half the absolute weight changes, `sum |w - current| / 2`:
0.2 allows 20% of the portfolio to be bought (and, equally, sold).

costs.description:
Costs per unit of weight traded, one per asset, in the units of the expected returns.
They reduce the expected return of objectives that use one.

quadratic_costs.description:
Costs that grow with the square of the weight traded, one per asset, such as the market
impact of large trades: `sum k_i (w_i - current_i)^2`, in the units of the expected
returns. They reduce the expected return of mean–variance, robust mean–variance and
target volatility objectives.

Turnover.description: Trading from the current portfolio: a limit on turnover, costs of trading, or both.

oneOf.description: An amount of money in a currency.
A return, weight or share as a fraction: 0.05 is 5%.
A ratio, such as a Sharpe ratio or a beta.
The level of an index, such as the growth of 100.
A count.

Unit.description: What the numbers of a series, grid or column measure.

oneOf.description:
Weights fitted once to the whole history and tested on it: what the strategy would have
done with perfect knowledge of the period. The default.

start.description: The first date of the test.

oneOf.description:
Weights fitted once to the history before `start`, and tested on the history from
`start` on.

years.description: The years of history each refit uses, such as 5.

periods.description: The periods of history each refit uses, such as 60 months, in place of `years`.

expanding.description:
Whether each refit uses all the history so far (`true`) rather than only the last
window (`false`, the default). The first fit still waits for a full window.

oneOf.description:
Weights refitted at each scheduled rebalance (monthly, quarterly, yearly or every so many
periods) on the window of history before it, and held until the next: every return in
the test comes after the weights were chosen. The window is given in years or in
periods.

Validation.description:
How a strategy's weights are tested: on the history they were fitted to, or on later
history they had not seen.

ValidationReport.description:
Every problem found while validating an input, rather than only the first.

Each issue carries a path that locates it in the input, so that a user interface can point
to the exact field.

positions.description: The positions, by account and instrument.

cash.description: The cash balances, by account and currency.

total_base.description: Positions and cash, in the base currency.

warnings.description: Prices and rates carried forward from earlier dates, and cash balances below zero.

Valuation.description: The holdings valued on a date.

values.description: The value of the portfolio at the end of each date.

flows.description:
The external flows since the previous date (deposits and transfers in positive;
withdrawals and transfers out negative), each converted at its own date's rate.

warnings.description: Prices and rates carried forward from earlier dates.

ValueSeries.description: Daily values and external flows in the base currency, the input to performance measurement.

portfolio.description:
The view portfolio: each asset's weight in it, such as `{"A": 1}` for an absolute view on
asset A, or `{"A": 1, "B": -1}` for a view that A outperforms B.

expected_return.description: The expected return of the view portfolio, in the units of the covariance matrix.

View.description: A view: the expected return of a portfolio of assets.

oneOf.description:
Proportional to the variance of the view portfolio, `tau * p' C p` (He and Litterman,
1999).

confidence.description: The confidence, greater than 0 and at most 1.

oneOf.description:
From a confidence in the view (Idzorek, 2005), as `(1 - c) / c * tau * p' C p`: 1 holds the
view with certainty, 0.5 is the proportional uncertainty, and lower confidences move the
posterior less.
The variance of the view, given directly.

ViewUncertainty.description: How uncertain a view is: its variance in the model.

asset.description: The asset, or the risk-free asset for cash.

proposed.description: Its weight in the weights found.

change.description: `proposed - current`: bought when positive, sold when negative.

cash.description: Whether this is the cash: the risk-free asset, or what the weights leave.

WeightChange.description: One asset's weight now and in the weights found.

date.description: The date at whose end the weights were bought.

WeightsAt.description: Weights at a date, by asset; what they leave is held in cash.

lower_returns.description: Every simulated month's return a percentage point a year lower.

crash.description:
The worst twelve months of the history placed before the target's date or at the first
payment, in every simulation; absent with less than twelve months to place them in.

WhatIf.description: The plan when markets do worse than the simulations assume.

start.description:
The valuation the year's return starts from: the last one of the year before, or the
first valuation.

end.description: The last valuation of the year.

complete.description: Whether the valuations cover the whole year.

YearReturn.description: The return of one calendar year (or the part of it covered).
